record.paper_title: Open problems originated in our research work with Zoltán Daróczy
record.original_question: Fix 1<q<2 and write θ=1/q. For a parameter η\in[θ,θ^2/(1-θ)], define the level-η regular expansion of x by iterating the rule x=ε_1(x)θ+θx_1 with binary digit ε_1(x)=0 for x\in[0,η) and ε_1(x)=1 for x\in[η,qη). For η_1<η_2 in this interval, let H(η_1,η_2) be the set of points whose level-η_1 and level-η_2 expansions are identical. Must H(η_1,η_2) always have Lebesgue measure zero?

evidence.quote: Regular expansion of level η : Let x ∈ I(1) η . Then x = ε1(x)θ + θx1, ε 1(x) ∈ A 1, x 1 ∈ I(1) η ; ε1(x) = 0, if x ∈ [0, η) ; 1, if x ∈ [η, qη).

Conjecture 6. Let η1 < η 2, η1, η2 ∈ [θ, θL]. Let H(η1, η2) be the set of those x ∈ [0, L] for which their expansions of level η1 and of level η2 are the same. Then the Lebesgue measure of H(η1, η2) is zero.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $1<q<2$ and set $\theta=1/q$. Fix a parameter $\eta\in[\theta,\ \theta^2/(1-\theta)]$, and let $L=\theta\eta/(1-\theta)$ (so that $q\eta = \eta + \theta L$ when $\eta=\theta L/(1-\theta)\cdot(1-\theta)/\theta$; more concretely, work on the natural invariant interval $I_\eta=[0,L]$ that contains $[0,q\eta)$). 

For $x\in[0,q\eta)$, define the level-$\eta$ regular expansion by the iteration
$$x = \varepsilon_1(x)\,\theta + \theta\, x_1,\qquad \varepsilon_n(x)\in\{0,1\},\ x_n\in[0,q\eta),$$
where the digit is determined by
$$\varepsilon_1(x)=\begin{cases}0,& x\in[0,\eta),\\ 1,& x\in[\eta,q\eta),\end{cases}$$
and $x_1=(x-\varepsilon_1(x)\theta)/\theta$; iterate this rule to obtain the digit sequence $(\varepsilon_n(x))_{n\ge 1}\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$.

Now let $\eta_1<\eta_2$ both lie in $[\theta,\ \theta^2/(1-\theta)]$, and define
$$H(\eta_1,\eta_2)=\bigl\{x:\ \varepsilon_n^{(\eta_1)}(x)=\varepsilon_n^{(\eta_2)}(x)\ \text{for every }n\ge 1\bigr\},$$
i.e. the set of points whose level-$\eta_1$ and level-$\eta_2$ regular expansions coincide as binary sequences.

Prove or disprove: for every such pair $\eta_1<\eta_2$, the Lebesgue measure of $H(\eta_1,\eta_2)$ is zero.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for this conjecture on level-$\eta$ regular expansions and the Lebesgue measure of the coincidence set $H(\eta_1,\eta_2)$ did not return any source confirming a proof or disproof. The conjecture appears to remain unresolved in the publicly indexed literature, but no authoritative recent survey was located to confirm its current status.
